items.title: 56800_John Simmons oral history interview
items.q: and the drummer's name was Daniels

ctx.x: They just kept playing without pay?

Two weeks. He just kept giving them [Mime] stories, and then I went back to the Moemoe, the four pieces. Then my next job was in San Diego, at the -- what is it? The hotel nightclub downstairs. Ramsey owned the hotel. I'm trying to think of the club that was downstairs. What's the name of it? Well, anyway, I worked in the club, and the leader of the group was a pianist named Nat Walker. And then we had Wee Willie, the alto player that worked with the Honeydrippers, and the drummer's name was Daniels, can't…

Then something happened to Nat, and he wigged out. He says, "Why didn't you all let me know that you didn't want me to be the leader of the band?" So they had to send him back to Los Angeles. They sent the Honeydripper down to take his place, and he took the band over. And the drummer left, and Davey Lewis, out of Kansas City, he was the drummer. He played drums, trumpet, two-finger piano like Lionel Hampton, and the vibes. And through the years, there's been a contro-
